I've been farming this land in Quzhou for half a century. I know its rhythms — the dry springs, the summer rains that come but aren't enough, the sandy loam that drains fast and needs feeding. At my age, my son helps when he's back from the city, but mostly I manage the 8 mu myself. I keep it simple: 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation I've always done, and 3 mu of cotton for cash income.

**Wheat:** I'll plant the usual 5 mu this October with the Jimai 22 variety — I switched to it ten years ago and the yield has been steady. I'll rotary-till after maize harvest, apply base fertilizer, then top-dress at jointing. Three irrigations: the winter water in December to protect roots, the jointing water in April, and a heading water in May if it's dry, which it usually is. Two pesticide applications — one for powdery mildew, one for aphids near heading.

**Maize:** Same 5 mu right after wheat harvest in June. I no-till and direct-seed hybrid Zhengdan 958 — saves my back and holds soil moisture. One base application, one topdress at the big flare stage. Two irrigations: one at establishment if it doesn't rain, one at silking. It almost always rains enough in July and August, but I've been burned before. Two pesticide sprays — mainly for corn borer.

**Cotton:** The 3 mu on the south end of my plot. I've grown Bt hybrid cotton for years, so I can cut way back on insecticide. Still need 4 irrigations — cotton is thirsty. I plough this field every year to turn in the old stalks. Four pesticide applications still, mostly for spider mites and aphid pressure in dry years.

I won't experiment with anything new this year. At 76, with only two of us at home and the labor costs what they are, I optimize for reliability, not maximum yield.
